entries.claim: A product search publishes names, bodies, and deep in order with deduplicated source-tagged results.
Deep search finds an authenticated metadata-selected item that name and body keyword search missed.
Large metadata scans stop at the fixed record bound while current-item progress remains coalesced.
Provider input exhaustion stops before a body read and does not advertise an unusable continuation.
The public event contract exposes only bounded stage metadata and SourceRef fields, including truthful skipped terminals.
entries.command: jq -e '.state == "pass" and .initial_plan == ["names:queued", "bodies:queued", "deep:queued"] and .public_projection.body_excerpt_is_public == false and .consumer_contract.terminal_predecessor_allows_later_skipped == true' docs/evidence/artifacts/issue-643/event-contract.json

entries.claim: Product readiness uses the real StoreArchive progressive executor rather than the minimal stub.
Unix archive body reads reject hardlinks before reading content.
The protected Windows job executed native archive handle and reparse-point tests on windows-latest.
Tool-shaped text read from an untrusted body cannot directly create a destructive tool action.
The one all-exit finalizer closes every opened progressive stage for every turn outcome.
Encrypted legacy recovery verifies the original object and semantic digests before migration.
The deterministic synthetic probe records a keyword-less deep hit, ordered activity, and one resolvable source without private content.
entries.command: jq -e '.state == "pass" and .fixture_kind == "synthetic" and .progressive_search.keywordless_selection_observed == true and .progressive_search.all_sources_resolved == true and .redaction.body_or_snippet_included == false' docs/evidence/artifacts/issue-643/deterministic-search-matrix.json
